title: Tesla's new FSD screen makes an AI video of the road as you drive
excerpt: Tesla's coming FSD screen uses AI video generation to create a drone-like view of the road. It's also showing drivers what the car plans to do.
content_html:
By Ben Shimkus

You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.

2026-11-23T20:51:49.778Z

Tesla's next FSD screen looks like it is projecting a drone shot. There is no drone.

On November 21, Tesla opened limited access to its latest semi-autonomous driving software — FSD (Supervised) v15 — to select customers. It's the first major consumer update in more than a year.

Tesla says it's substantially safer. CEO Elon Musk has compared its Reality View visuals to playing a video game.

FSD v15 now starting to roll out – upgrading every part of the end-to-end driving network Safety 25x better handling of safety critical cases Tesla Reality View Adds a live visualization of the drive that lets you see & control what FSD is planning to do Navigation for start & end of the trip now learns end-to-end from fleet route preferences. Later v15 releases will expand this to the entire route. You also should notice better detection of signs, animals, debris, potholes and standing water, plus more natural speed handling in school zones and inclement weather. Lastly, FSD can now slow for speed cameras & Bike Rack Mode lets you enable FSD w/ bike racks or similar hitch accessories

— Tesla (@Tesla) November 21, 2026

The screen used to show a simplified Tesla on a white road, with gray blocks for nearby vehicles. Now, it depicts surrounding traffic, crosswalks, buildings, and floating arrows that mark the route ahead.

"It's like GTA," Musk posted on X on Saturday, before writing, "This is real-time AI video generation (no gaming engine!) using just half of one AI4 TRIP accelerator."

In another (classically Musk-ian, nerdy) post, he explained that the car's cameras feed the same vision system that helps produce FSD's driving actions. Tesla then branches off that visual information into a separate model that generates the video-like view on the screen.

While the video feed and arrows give Tesla a gamified new look, Ashok Elluswamy, the automaker's VP of AI software, said the system "communicates the intent of the car."

Reality View is the splashiest part of v15. Tesla also claims the update improves navigation, parking, pothole avoidance, and detection of animals and road debris. It says the update improves its "safety critical cases" by 25x, but Tesla has not explained that metric or released supporting data.

FSD remains a supervised driver-assistance system — drivers must keep their eyes on the road and be prepared to take over if the system makes a mistake.
